title: 📘 UNIT 6: HUMAN–NATURAL ENVIRONMENT INTERACTIONS
notes: 🌍 Human–natural environment interaction :- the relationship between people and the natural environment through dependence, modification, and adaptation.

title: 6.1 👥 OVERVIEW OF GLOBAL POPULATION CHANGE
notes:
👥 Population change → the difference in population size between the beginning and end of a given period.

📈 Population growth → an increase in the number of individuals in a population.

➕ Population increases through → fertility (birth) + immigration (in-migration).

➖ Population decreases through → mortality (death) + emigration (out-migration).

🔄 Population composition can change through → birth and death rates, sex ratio, life expectancy, and migration.

📊 Importance → understanding population trends helps governments plan for education, healthcare, employment, housing, food, water, energy, and other development needs.

🌍 Global trend → world population growth accelerated greatly during the 20th century, particularly in developing regions.

🇪🇹 Africa → Sub-Saharan Africa experienced population stagnation from about 1500–1900, followed by very rapid growth during the 20th century.

⛓️ Causes of African population stagnation (1500–1900) → slave trade, colonization, and widespread deadly diseases.

📉 Population in Africa → increased only from about 80 million in 1500 to about 100 million in 1900, while several other world regions experienced much greater growth.

🚀 Demographic explosion → rapid population growth experienced by developing regions during the 20th century.

🌍 Sub-Saharan Africa → population growth averaged about 2.8% per year during 1900–1980.

📈 1980–2015 → Eastern Africa averaged about 2.9% growth, Central Africa about 3.0%, Western Africa about 2.7%, while Southern Africa had a lower rate of about 1.8%.

💡 Main reasons for recent population growth → advances in modern medicine, improved living standards, reduced infant/child/maternal mortality, and increased life expectancy.

🌱 Sustainable development → rapid population growth creates challenges for employment, income distribution, poverty reduction, healthcare, education, housing, sanitation, water, food, and energy.

title: 6.1.1 🌍 GLOBAL POPULATION DISTRIBUTION
notes:
🌏 Asia → the world's most populous continent.

🌍 Africa → the second most populous continent and one of the world's fastest-growing population regions.

📊 2021 population shares → Asia about 59.54%, Africa about 17.20%, Europe about 9.59%, North America about 7.60%, South America about 5.53%, and Oceania about 0.55%.

🔥 Key point → Asia and Africa together accounted for about 77% of the world's population in 2021.

⚠️ Population pressure → rapid growth increases the demand for resources and public services, making effective planning and sustainable resource use essential.

title: 6.2 🌱 HUMAN–ENVIRONMENT RELATIONSHIP
notes:
🌱 Environment → the surroundings or conditions in which people, animals, and plants live or operate. It includes the external factors affecting living organisms.

🤝 Human–environment relationship → a two-way relationship in which humans affect the environment and the environment affects humans.

🎯 Purpose of interaction → humans interact with the environment mainly to satisfy their increasing needs.

🔑 Three major forms of interaction → Dependence, Modification, and Adaptation.

title: 6.2.1 🏞️ DEPENDENCE ON THE ENVIRONMENT
notes:
🌍 Human dependence → people depend on environmental resources for survival and economic activities.

🍚 Food → soil, plants, and animals provide food for humans.

💧 Water → obtained from rainfall, rivers, lakes, and oceans; used for drinking, washing, irrigation, and power generation.

🏠 Shelter → materials such as sand, stone, and timber are obtained from the environment.

👕 Clothing → natural materials such as cotton and silk provide raw materials for clothing.

⛏️ Economic resources → water, timber, minerals, and other natural resources provide inputs for production.

🌿 Ecosystem services → nature contributes through water purification, flood-risk management, carbon sequestration, and nutrient cycling.

♻️ Key idea → natural resources support both present and future human needs, so they must be used sustainably.

title: 6.2.2 🏗️ MODIFICATION OF THE ENVIRONMENT
notes:
🏗️ Environmental modification → changing the natural environment to satisfy human needs and obtain resources.

🌳 Deforestation → forests may be cleared to increase agricultural land and crop production.

💧 Dams → constructed for hydroelectric power, irrigation, water storage, and flood control.

🛢️ Resource extraction → drilling and mining modify the physical environment to obtain natural resources.

⚠️ Negative effects → overpopulation, pollution, fossil-fuel burning, deforestation, climate change, soil erosion, poor air quality, and contaminated water.

🌪️ Environmental hazards → floods, droughts, wildfires, earthquakes, and tsunamis can negatively affect people and may cause migration and loss of life.

🌳 Positive modification → afforestation and conservation can improve environmental conditions, reduce carbon dioxide, improve air quality, and protect endangered species.

⚖️ Key idea → human modification can be beneficial or harmful depending on how resources are used.

title: 6.2.3 🌡️ ADAPTATION TO ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGES
notes:
🌡️ Adaptation → adjustment to a new or changing environment to improve human survival.

🎯 Purpose → reduce vulnerability, reduce exposure to environmental impacts, build adaptive capacity, and support sustainable development.

⚠️ Environmental changes → climate change, deforestation, desertification, floods, droughts, and other environmental stresses can require adaptation.

🤝 Adaptation process → identify vulnerability → analyze present and future impacts → design strategies → implement actions → monitor and evaluate → share knowledge and lessons.

🛠️ Adaptation responses → technological solutions (grey measures), ecosystem-based solutions (green measures), and behavioral, managerial, and policy approaches (soft measures).

🌳 Green measures → nature-based solutions such as reforestation that can reduce desertification and help recharge groundwater.

💻 Grey measures → technological and infrastructure-based solutions that may require greater funding, research, training, and technical knowledge.

📋 Soft measures → behavioral, managerial, institutional, and policy changes that strengthen people's ability to cope with environmental changes.

title: 6.2.4 🔄 TYPES OF ADAPTATION
notes:
⚡ Autonomous adaptation → adaptation that occurs without a conscious policy decision; it is triggered by ecological, market, lifestyle, or other changes.

🌱 Spontaneous adaptation → another term used for autonomous adaptation.

📋 Planned adaptation → deliberate adaptation resulting from a policy or decision made after recognizing that environmental conditions have changed or are expected to change.

🏠 Examples → building houses on higher ground to avoid floods, using natural slopes for irrigation, wearing thin clothes in hot climates, and wearing warm clothes in cold climates.

❗ Key idea → humans cannot modify every environmental condition; where modification is impossible, adaptation becomes necessary.

title: 6.2.5 🧠 ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINISM VS POSSIBILISM
notes:
🌍 Environmental determinism → the idea that the physical environment strongly controls or shapes human activities, cultures, and economic development.

📌 Historical view → environmental determinism was widely promoted by European thinkers during the 19th century but was later rejected.

🌎 Environmental possibilism → the idea that the environment provides limitations and opportunities, but humans can choose among different possibilities and adapt using knowledge and technology.

⚙️ Technology and modernization → as technological advancement and modernization increase, humans can overcome more environmental limitations.

🔑 Difference → Determinism emphasizes environmental control; Possibilism emphasizes human choice and adaptation.

title: 6.3 🌿 INDIGENOUS KNOWLEDGE IN CONSERVATION OF NATURAL RESOURCES IN AFRICA
notes:
🌿 Indigenous knowledge → knowledge, skills, beliefs, and practices developed by indigenous communities through long interaction with their environment and passed from generation to generation.

🌍 Importance → indigenous knowledge contributes to biodiversity conservation, environmental management, sustainable resource use, and adaptation to local environmental conditions.

🌱 Biological resources → African communities depend on plants and animals for food, construction materials, medicine, and other needs.

🌿 Traditional medicine → plant medicine has long been important in Africa because of local availability, affordability, cultural acceptance, and limited access to modern healthcare in some rural areas.

🧠 Local knowledge → African communities possess extensive knowledge about biodiversity and the uses of different plants and animals.

♻️ Conservation role → traditional beliefs, rules, customs, and community practices can protect forests, water resources, wildlife, and other natural resources.

⚠️ Environmental degradation → indigenous knowledge can help reduce unsustainable resource use and support sustainable management.

title: 📚 UNIT 6 SUMMARY
notes:
👥 Population change → affected by births, deaths, and migration; population growth is especially rapid in Sub-Saharan Africa.

🌍 Africa → experienced population stagnation from 1500–1900 because of slave trade, colonization, and deadly diseases, followed by rapid growth in the 20th century.

🌱 Human–environment interaction → occurs through dependence, modification, and adaptation.

🏞️ Dependence → humans obtain food, water, shelter, clothing, raw materials, and ecosystem services from nature.

🏗️ Modification → humans change the environment to satisfy their needs, producing both positive and negative effects.

🌡️ Adaptation → humans adjust to environmental changes through autonomous or planned responses.

🧠 Environmental theories → determinism emphasizes environmental control, while possibilism emphasizes human choices and technological possibilities.

🌿 Indigenous knowledge → African communities have developed valuable traditional practices for conserving biodiversity and natural resources.

⚖️ Central idea → humans depend on and modify the environment, but sustainable use and conservation are essential for long-term survival and development.

title: 📝 UNIT 6: EXAM QUICK REVIEW
notes:
🔹 Population change = difference in population size over time.

🔹 Population increase = births + immigration.

🔹 Population decrease = deaths + emigration.

🔹 Three human–environment interactions = dependence + modification + adaptation.

🔹 Dependence = obtaining necessities and resources from the environment.

🔹 Modification = changing the environment to satisfy human needs.

🔹 Adaptation = adjusting to environmental conditions for survival.

🔹 Autonomous adaptation = spontaneous, non-policy-driven response.

🔹 Planned adaptation = deliberate response based on a decision or policy.

🔹 Determinism = environment strongly controls human activities.

🔹 Possibilism = humans can choose among possibilities and adapt using knowledge and technology.

🔹 Indigenous knowledge = locally developed knowledge and practices passed through generations.

🔹 Main conservation lesson = combine useful indigenous practices with sustainable resource management.
